title: Live-cell imaging of PVD dendritic growth cone in post-embryonic C. elegans
protocol: Start with synchronized L1 larvae obtained by bleaching gravid adult transgenic C. elegans.
Hatch the embryos in M9 buffer one day before the experiment.
Pick 20 transgenic C. elegans at L4 stage with expression of GFP or LifeAct::NeonGreen in PVD neurons on each feeding NGM plate (5.5 cm).
Distribute 20 worms onto four plates (5 per plate) for each experiment.
Cultivate the worms for 3 days at 20°C.
Wash down C. elegans with 1 mL M9 buffer per plate.
Collect hermaphrodites into a single 15 mL glass tube.
Centrifuge at 1500 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 10 mL of M9 Buffer to wash the sample.
Repeat washing steps until the supernatant becomes clear.
Remove the supernatant, resuspend the worm pellet with alkaline-bleach solution.
Seal the opening with parafilm.
Place the 15 mL glass tube on a rocking plate and gently rock for no longer than 5 min.
Visually inspect the worm-containing solution against room light to ensure that worm carcasses are gone.
Stop the reaction by adding 10 mL M9 buffer after soaking in bleach for up to 7 minutes.
Centrifuge at 4000 × g for 5 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Wash the embryos with M9 buffer as step 5, repeating this step three times.
Resuspend the embryos in 1 mL M9 buffer and seal the opening with parafilm.
Incubate the embryos without bacterial food at 20°C for 12–16 hours on a rocker.
Centrifuge the arrested L1 larvae at 1500 × g for 5 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the larvae in 50 μL M9 buffer.
Drop 2–5 μL worm solution onto NGM plates seeded with OP50 bacteria.
Cultivate the L1 larvae for 20 hours at 20°C.
Drop the levamisole/Microbeads mixture on the gel pad.
Pick animals into the solution.
Seal the edge of the coverslip with 3M tape.
Trim the 3M tape to fit the slide.
Tape two glass slides with lab tape.
Use a Pasteur pipette to put a drop of freshly melted 10% (w/v) agarose onto the center of the untapped slide.
Lay another untaped slide on the melted gel perpendicular to the third slide and press gently.
Wait for 10 seconds until the gel pad is cool down.
Carefully remove the fourth slide by sliding it.
Use a razor blade to trim the pad to fit the size slightly smaller than the coverslip.
Prepare the anesthetic mixture by mixing 1 μL of 5% (w/v) levamisole, 0.25 μL of liquid OP50 culture at 0.4–0.6 optical density, and 0.75 μL of microbeads.
Place around 10 synchronized L2 C. elegans larvae in the anesthetic mixture.
Wait for 2 minutes until the movements of larvae are significantly reduced.
Put on the coverslip.
Gently seal the edge of the coverslip by vaseline or 3M tape.
Place the slide on the microscope stage and search for transgenic C. elegans under the 10× objective.
Image growth cone morphology under the 63× objective.
Set the laser intensity at 20% and exposure time at 200 ms as default settings.
Adjust the exposure time and laser intensity until the dendritic growth cone is clearly observed.
Locate the PVD cell body first, then move horizontally to locate the growth cone of the horizontal primary dendrite.
Alternatively, use the ALA axon as a landmark to locate the PVD dendritic growth cone.
Acquire z-stack images of the dendritic growth cone under the 63× objective by spinning-disk confocal microscope at 2-min intervals for up to 4 hours.
Search another animal if the growth cone arrests for more than 30 min during imaging.
Discard the slide when imaging time exceeds 5 hours.
Obtain maximal projection images of the z-series by Zen software (Carl Zeiss).
Import sequential images into Fiji (ImageJ) to produce videos.
